title: arxiv_2403.15712v1
universal_lens: The structural unification of multi-modal object tracking is formalized via a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes represent latent feature states and edges correspond to differentiable operators. The architecture search optimizes edge weights, effectively discovering the optimal kernel for state transitions across image and LiDAR modalities.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the DAG acts as a conformal prediction network. Edge weights are treated as Bayesian priors over operator efficacy. Latency constraints define the calibration sets, ensuring that the inferred player trajectories maintain strict coverage probabilities under varying sensor noise distributions.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes this primitive for real-time situational reasoning. The normal and reduction cells map directly to micro-state transitions in gameplay. Shared parameters enforce cross-modal consistency, allowing the engine to seamlessly fuse optical tracking with spatial telemetry during high-velocity state changes.

primitives.name: Neural Architecture Search Pareto Frontier
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, we explore the use of the neural architecture search (NAS) methods to search for efficient architectures for tracking, aiming for low real-time latency while maintaining relatively high accuracy.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a trade-off surface exists between model complexity (latency) and tracking performance (accuracy).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the Pareto frontier becomes non-convex due to conflicting modalities.

layer2.mapping: Maps Pareto optimal architectures to GSI's multi-objective risk management framework, where latency corresponds to transaction settlement time and accuracy maps to predictive certainty.
layer2.telemetry: Measured inference latency in milliseconds and tracking mean average precision (mAP) on edge hardware.

primitives.name: Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Another challenge for object tracking is the unreliability of a single sensor, therefore, we propose a multi-modal framework to improve the robustness.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent sensor noise models and synchronized temporal data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when sensor data fails to align temporally or spatially.

layer2.mapping: Maps sensor fusion to GSE's state-transition graphs, where each sensor provides a distinct observation kernel that updates the belief state over possible player positions.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-modal association accuracy and consistency metrics across LiDAR, camera, and radar inputs.

primitives.name: Tracking-by-Detection Paradigm
primitives.verbatim_quote: Initially, a pre-trained detector is employed to procure object detections, after which a tracker undertakes the data association task, assigning a distinct ID to each detected object across successive frames.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent object instances and Markovian transition dynamics between frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks when object identities change unpredictably or when the scene becomes fully occluded.

layer2.mapping: Maps detection-confidence scores to GSI's posterior probability estimates in conformal prediction, while data association links correspond to GSE's action-selection policies.
layer2.telemetry: Identity preservation rate and false positive/negative counts per frame.

primitives.name: Pareto Optimal Latency Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: Experiments demonstrate that our algorithm can run on edge devices within lower latency constraints, thus greatly reducing the computational requirements for multi-modal object tracking while keeping lower latency.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a fixed upper bound on acceptable latency for real-time operation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks when the constraint is violated, causing system instability.

layer2.mapping: Maps the latency ceiling to GSE's decision horizon, where the tracker must complete its update before the next state transition, while GSI uses similar thresholds to control market exposure duration.
layer2.telemetry: Maximum observed inference time per frame and percentage of frames meeting the latency target.

primitives.name: Multi-Modal Feature Fusion Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: A fusion module is then used to fuse the multi-modal features.
primitives.assumptions: Features from different modalities are assumed to be spatially aligned and temporally synchronized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when sensor calibration errors cause misalignment between modalities.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian fusion in GSI / conformal prediction combination in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Cross-modal mutual information or consistency score between fused and ground-truth features

primitives.name: Correlation Feature Calculation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The fused features are split into tracklet features and detection features, from which the correlation features can be calculated.
primitives.assumptions: Euclidean inner product assumes linear feature space; non-linearity may require kernelized variants.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity when tracklet/detection vectors become orthogonal, leading to zero correlation.

layer2.mapping: Kernelized association metrics in GSI / similarity-based track merging in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Average correlation magnitude per tracklet over batches; drop below threshold indicates poor matches

primitives.name: Adjacent Estimator Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: These features are input to the following adjacent estimator to infer confidence and affinity scores.
primitives.assumptions: Separable estimation functions assume independent impact of correlation on confidence vs. affinity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting occurs when estimators learn noise instead of true association patterns.

layer2.mapping: Probabilistic assignment in GSI / sequential decision-making in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall curve on inferred associations; area under curve quantifies estimator quality

primitives.name: Linear Programming State Update Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: At last, linear programming is used to update the new tracklets from the inferred scores.
primitives.assumptions: Global optimality relies on convex relaxation; integrality gap exists for large-scale problems.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degeneracy arises when multiple assignments yield identical minimal cost.

layer2.mapping: Optimal transport in GSI / min-cost flow network in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Number of tracklet switches per sequence; low switching indicates stable updates

primitives.name: Latency-Constrained Architecture Search
primitives.verbatim_quote: In order to search for an efficient network structure with a low inference time, we add a latency constraint to the loss function for the first stage.
primitives.assumptions: The network architecture is represented as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes correspond to intermediate feature maps and edges represent candidate operations. The latency constraint assumes a linear relationship between computational complexity and inference time on the target hardware.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the latency budget is too tight, the search space may become infeasible, leading to suboptimal architectures with degraded tracking performance.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian optimization over discrete architectural parameters, where posterior distributions over latency and MOTA metrics inform sequential decision-making.
layer2.telemetry: Reciprocal of latency (1/s) vs. MOTA (%) on KITTI testing dataset

primitives.name: Pruning Low-Weight Operations
primitives.verbatim_quote: Therefore, we will remove the operations with low weight to reduce the size of the model.
primitives.assumptions: The weights associated with each operation can be interpreted as their contribution to the final prediction; pruning thresholds are determined via magnitude-based selection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Aggressive pruning may cause catastrophic forgetting, resulting in a disconnected DAG where information flow between nodes is disrupted.

layer2.mapping: Conformal pruning filters out redundant latent variables, reducing the state-space dimensionality while maintaining predictive coverage.
layer2.telemetry: Number of remaining operations vs. MOTA degradation on validation set

primitives.name: Gap-Filling Training
primitives.verbatim_quote: As a result, we continue to train the pruned model to get the best tracking network.
primitives.assumptions: The pruned model's initial parameters are fine-tuned using the same loss function as the first stage, assuming that local optima are connected in parameter space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient fine-tuning may leave the pruned architecture stuck in poor local minima, negating the benefits of early pruning.

layer2.mapping: Transfer learning across training epochs, where knowledge from earlier stages is transferred to later stages through continued gradient descent.
layer2.telemetry: Fine-tuning loss curve convergence vs. number of epochs

primitives.name: Latency-Benchmark Comparison
primitives.verbatim_quote: Accuracy on KITTI Benchmark Our model is trained and evaluated on the KITTI Benchmark [12], which consists of 29 testing sequences and 21 training sequences.
primitives.assumptions: The KITTI dataset provides a standardized testbed with consistent camera intrinsics and ground truth annotations, allowing for fair cross-method comparison.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance on KITTI may not generalize to other domains with vastly different lighting, scale, or object categories.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian ranking of models based on joint posterior distributions of MOTA and latency, accounting for uncertainty in empirical estimates.
layer2.telemetry: Ranking of methods by expected utility (MOTA - λ·latency) under prior beliefs about trade-off parameter λ

primitives.name: Differentiable Architecture Search Topology
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each cell consists of N nodes, where each edge between two nodes represents an operation in a pre-defined search space.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: Number of nodes (dimensionless integer). Edge: Directed connection representing a specific convolution or pooling operator (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The underlying feature transformation can be decomposed into a finite set of discrete operations connected linearly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the operational complexity exceeds the expressivity of the predefined search space, leading to suboptimal local minima.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's tactical decision tree, where nodes are game states and edges are valid player actions constrained by rules.
layer2.telemetry: Graph density and average path length within the discovered neural cell.

primitives.name: Dual-Modality Feature Branching
primitives.verbatim_quote: In our designed architecture, there are two branches in the feature extraction backbone, one is image modality, and the other one is LiDAR modality.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Image Modality: 2D pixel intensity arrays (dimensionless normalized units). LiDAR Modality: 3D point cloud spatial coordinates (meters).
primitives.assumptions: Both modalities provide complementary information about the same underlying physical entity without severe temporal misalignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under extreme occlusion in one modality if the fusion mechanism lacks robust fallback heuristics.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's dual-stream inference engine fusing broadcast video with on-field wearable GPS data for holistic athlete tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-correlation coefficient between image-derived and LiDAR-derived bounding boxes.

primitives.name: Feature Channel Reduction Cell
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each branch, the network consists of two different kinds of cell, normal cell and reduction cell, where the former one does not change the feature channels while the latter one does.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Feature Channels: Dimensionality of the latent vector space (dimensionless). Normal Cell: Identity mapping on channel dimension. Reduction Cell: Down-sampling operator.
primitives.assumptions: Spatial resolution reduction is necessary to increase the receptive field and capture global contextual dependencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive reduction leads to irreversible loss of fine-grained spatial details required for precise boundary delineation.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's macro-to-micro state aggregation, reducing high-frequency positional updates into strategic zone occupancies.
layer2.telemetry: Channel dimensionality ratio before and after the reduction cell.

primitives.name: Shared Architectural Parameters
primitives.verbatim_quote: Notably, the searched architecture parameters α are shared by cells of both branches.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: α: Continuous architectural weights governing edge selection probabilities (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The fundamental topological structure of feature extraction is invariant across different sensory inputs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated if the distinct modalities require fundamentally disjoint computational graphs due to vastly different signal frequencies.

layer2.mapping: Derives GSI's unified player identity kernel, enforcing consistent tracking IDs regardless of whether the input is visual or radar-based.
layer2.telemetry: Gradient alignment metric between the image and LiDAR branches during backpropagation.

reasoning_traces.think: The chapter window introduces a sophisticated Neural Architecture Search (NAS) framework tailored for Multi-Object Tracking (MOT). The core mathematical innovation lies in parameterizing the network topology itself. By defining a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) where nodes are feature vectors and edges are weighted operations from a discrete search space (e.g., separable convolutions, pooling), the authors transform structural design into a continuous optimization problem. This is heavily inspired by DARTS, utilizing gradient descent to update edge weights (α). The introduction of 'normal' and 'reduction' cells allows the model to dynamically manage spatial resolution and feature depth. Crucially, the architecture employs a dual-branch system for image and LiDAR modalities. The profound theoretical leap here is the sharing of architectural parameters α across these disparate branches. This implies a deep structural isomorphism between how visual pixels and spatial point clouds should be processed to extract trackable entities. The optimization balances MOTA (tracking accuracy) against latency, explicitly navigating the Pareto frontier of computational efficiency versus predictive power. The final architecture is distilled by pruning edges below a weight threshold, yielding a sparse, highly efficient computational graph optimized for real-time deployment on hardware like the RTX 8000.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology traces its lineage directly to Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS), which revolutionized NAS by replacing expensive reinforcement learning with gradient-based optimization. It also inherits from multi-modal fusion paradigms in autonomous driving, where combining camera and LiDAR data is paramount. The use of separable convolutions harks back to MobileNet architectures, emphasizing the necessity of lightweight operators for real-time systems. The explicit trade-off analysis between MOTA and latency reflects the evolution of MOT from purely accuracy-driven metrics to deployment-aware engineering constraints.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the NAS algorithm acts as an adversarial agent attempting to discover the most efficient cognitive pathway for tracking. It anticipates the 'opponent'—the complex, noisy, and occluded nature of real-world scenes. By sharing parameters α, the model implicitly learns a universal 'theory of motion' that applies regardless of the sensory modality. It understands that whether observing through light (image) or laser pulses (LiDAR), the underlying kinematic principles of the tracked objects remain constant, thus enforcing a unified perceptual model across branches.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the shared parameters α force a suboptimal compromise between the two modalities. If the optimal topology for high-frequency LiDAR point clouds drastically differs from the low-frequency texture dependencies in images, forcing parameter sharing could induce catastrophic interference. Furthermore, the pruning threshold acts as a hard veto; if too many edges are discarded, the graph connectivity might break, isolating nodes and destroying the flow of gradient information during training, rendering the network incapable of learning long-range dependencies.
